correctness.rationale: The exact disk support values yield h(u)=sqrt(||u||_2^2-min_i(u_i^2)) at unit radius. Equality cases rigorously partition the exposed boundary into eight equilateral triangles and twenty-four congruent ruled patches, with residual input circle arcs of area zero. A patch parametrization F(phi,t)=(cos phi,t sin phi,(1-t) sin phi) has area Jacobian sin phi sqrt(1+sin^2 phi) and outward support height 1/sqrt(1+sin^2 phi). Evaluating its area integral and divergence flux, plus the exact triangle contributions, gives surface area 12-4 sqrt(3)+2 pi and volume 8-10 sqrt(2)/3; scaling is exact. The support minimum sqrt(2/3), central symmetry and unit circumsphere give both radii. A separate executable numerically verifies quadrature, support and 3D approximating hulls; this finite evidence is supplementary, not an infinite proof.

The closest algebraic hull work treats two circles. Cospherical disjoint-cap constructions exclude the overlapping great-circle caps here, and Steinmetz tables concern the polar tricylinder, not the present primal hull. Direct published literature, synonyms, exact constants and semantic research records provided no dominating theorem, although unindexed historical work and the full unavailable CHoCC article remain residual risks.

value.rationale: The convex hull of three mutually perpendicular equatorial disks is a canonical symmetric convex body and the polar of the classical tricylinder, but the known polar volume is not its intrinsic volume. The result simultaneously evaluates exact area and volume and exhaustively classifies an 8-triangle/24-developable-patch boundary arising from three-way support ties. These explicit structural invariants provide a natural benchmark for general circle-hull constructions and are not a textbook two-disk substitution or arbitrary parameter slice.
